questions.q: What is a "road" under the Traffic Ordinance?
options: Only a paved carriageway allocated for motor vehicle traffic
Any track, road, street, alley, square, passage or open place the public has a right to pass through
Any private land whose owner has allowed passage over it
Only a road that a local authority has declared an "urban road"
questions.explain: The definition in the Traffic Ordinance, section 1, is very broad and covers any place the public has a right to pass through — not just paved carriageways.

questions.q: What is the difference between a "carriageway" and the "shoulder"?
options: There is no difference — they are two names for the same part
The shoulder is only the part of the carriageway painted with a white line
The carriageway is the part for vehicle traffic; the shoulder is defined separately and is not a carriageway, even when it is paved
The carriageway exists only on an urban road, and the shoulder only on a non-urban road
questions.explain: Regulation 1 defines the carriageway as the part for vehicle traffic, "excluding the shoulder" — meaning the shoulder, even when paved, is not part of the carriageway.

questions.q: On a road with a built divider between the two directions of traffic, how is each carriageway on either side of the divider treated?
options: As two lanes of the same two-way carriageway
As the shoulder
As a one-way carriageway in its own right
As an area that is not part of the road at all
questions.explain: Under regulation 34, when there is a divider, each carriageway on either side of it is treated as a separate one-way carriageway — so you must not cross the divider or stop on it.

questions.q: What is an "interchange"?
options: A large traffic circle
A stretch of road with three or more lanes in each direction
Where roads meet at different levels, including the roads that connect them
An ordinary junction with a traffic light
questions.explain: Regulation 1 defines an interchange as where roads meet at different levels, including the connecting roads between them — unlike an intersection, which is a meeting at the same level.

questions.q: One of the conditions in the definition of an "expressway" is —
options: A permitted maximum speed of {{fact:speed.freeway}} on every stretch of it without exception
A lane width of at least 4 metres on every lane
At least two carriageways separated by a divider, with at least two lanes in each direction, no access from adjoining premises, and no intersections
The road's name begins with an even number
questions.explain: The definition in regulation 1 includes physical separation between the carriageways, at least two lanes per direction, no access from adjoining premises, and no intersections or railway crossings — only merges are allowed.

questions.q: What does regulation 25 require of a driver?
options: Only to hold a valid driving licence
To drive only on urban roads during their first year
To hold comprehensive insurance
To be competent in operating and using the vehicle
questions.explain: Regulation 25 states that no person shall drive a vehicle unless they are competent in operating and using it — a separate duty from simply holding a licence.

questions.q: A person is leading a bicycle by hand on the pavement, without disturbing other pedestrians. What is their status?
options: Absolutely forbidden, under any conditions
A cyclist in every respect, and forbidden to be on the pavement
They must get onto the carriageway and push the bicycle on the shoulder
It is allowed — for this purpose they count as a pedestrian
questions.explain: Regulation 129 allows a pedestrian to lead a bicycle on the pavement if this does not disturb other pedestrians, even though for most traffic rules they count as a cyclist (reg. 133).

questions.q: Who must not drive a vehicle under regulation 26?
options: Someone whose vehicle is an unusual colour
Someone driving on a non-urban road for the first time
Someone under the influence of intoxicating drugs or intoxicating drinks
Someone driving in the afternoon hours
questions.explain: Regulation 26 forbids driving by someone under the influence of drugs or alcohol, someone whose state endangers road users, and someone whose mental or physical state denies them control of the vehicle or a view of the road.

questions.q: A pedestrian wants to cross a road, and nearby there is both a pedestrian crossing and a junction with no crossing. What should they do?
options: Cross at the pedestrian crossing
Cross wherever is more convenient
Cross at the junction instead, because there they have priority
Wait for a vehicle to stop for them wherever they choose
questions.explain: When a pedestrian crossing, underpass or footbridge is nearby, the pedestrian must cross only there — and only in their absence should they cross near a junction.

questions.q: Who is responsible for making sure a minor passenger in a vehicle is wearing a seatbelt?
options: Only the parent, even if not in the vehicle
There is no such duty on anyone
Only the minor themselves
The driver
questions.explain: The driver is responsible for belting in minor passengers; full details are in the Seatbelts, child seats and passengers chapter.

questions.q: Under the Traffic Ordinance, which of the following count as a "vehicle"?
options: Only vehicles that have a registration plate
Only vehicles registered with the licensing authority
Only motor vehicles
Motor vehicles as well as bicycles
questions.explain: The definition in section 1 of the Ordinance explicitly includes "a bicycle and a tricycle," not only motor vehicles.

questions.q: What distinguishes a "commercial vehicle" from a "private vehicle"?
options: A commercial vehicle is always heavier than {{fact:licence.b.max_weight}}
A commercial vehicle is used to carry goods for hire or for its owner's business; a private vehicle is neither public nor commercial
A private vehicle cannot carry any cargo at all
The colour of the licence plate alone
questions.explain: The definitions depend on how the vehicle is used: a commercial vehicle is meant to carry goods for hire or for business purposes, and a private vehicle is any vehicle that is neither public nor commercial.

questions.q: A person riding a mobility scooter —
options: Must hold a category B driving licence
Must hold a category 1 driving licence only
Must hold a temporary driving licence until age 18
Is exempt from a driving licence and from vehicle registration
questions.explain: The owner and the rider of a mobility scooter are exempt from vehicle registration and licensing and from a driving licence, subject to age and fitness conditions.

questions.q: What is the minimum age for riding a mobility scooter?
options: There is no age limit for a mobility scooter
16 only for a disabled person, and 18 for everyone else
18 for everyone
{{fact:mobility_scooter.min_age}}, and for a disabled person — {{fact:mobility_scooter.min_age_disabled}}
questions.explain: Regulation 39I sets a minimum age of {{fact:mobility_scooter.min_age}}, and for a disabled person — {{fact:mobility_scooter.min_age_disabled}}, provided their physical and mental state allows safe operation.

questions.q: What defines a "work vehicle"?
options: Any vehicle owned by a company
A vehicle that carries workers to a worksite
A vehicle with work equipment permanently fitted, or whose structure is designed to perform work, and that is not intended to carry goods or passengers
A commercial vehicle over {{fact:licence.b.max_weight}} only
questions.explain: The definition focuses on purpose: permanent work equipment or a structure designed for work, as distinct from carrying goods or passengers.

questions.q: What is a vehicle's "kerb weight"?
options: The gross vehicle weight under the vehicle licence
The weight of the completely empty vehicle, without fuel and without oil
The weight of the vehicle with one driver only
The weight of the vehicle without cargo and without a driver, including the vehicle's fittings, fuel, water and oil
questions.explain: Kerb weight includes all the vehicle's fittings and the fluids in it (fuel, water, oil) — but not cargo and not a driver.

questions.q: What is the maximum gross vehicle weight for a vehicle driven on a category B driving licence?
options: {{fact:licence.b.max_weight}}
questions.explain: A B licence permits driving a vehicle whose gross vehicle weight is up to {{fact:licence.b.max_weight}}; above that a heavy licence is required.

questions.q: A driver of a commercial vehicle whose gross vehicle weight is over {{fact:alcohol.strict.weight_threshold}} is subject to —
options: Exemption from a sobriety test
The stricter alcohol threshold — {{fact:alcohol.strict.breath}} in breath
The ordinary alcohol threshold only
An absolute ban on driving after any drinking at all, with no test
questions.explain: Driving a commercial vehicle or work vehicle over {{fact:alcohol.strict.weight_threshold}} is subject to the stricter threshold of {{fact:alcohol.strict.breath}}, the same as a new driver.

questions.q: What is the risk from an unbalanced axle load, even when the vehicle's gross weight is within limits?
options: No risk at all — only the gross weight matters
Only higher fuel consumption
The vehicle will fail the annual test because of its colour
Impaired braking and steering due to the weight distribution between the axles
questions.explain: Even when the gross weight is within the permitted ceiling, an unbalanced load between the axles can impair braking and vehicle control.

questions.q: What determines the severity of the penalty for driving overloaded?
options: The type of vehicle alone
The number of passengers in the vehicle
The colour of the vehicle
The percentage by which the gross vehicle weight is exceeded
questions.explain: The greater the percentage by which the gross vehicle weight is exceeded, the more severe the penalty — from a fine and points up to immediate disqualification at {{fact:police.vehicle_ban.overload_pct}} or more.

questions.q: What is the difference between the Traffic Ordinance and the Traffic Regulations?
options: The Ordinance applies only to heavy vehicles
There is no difference — they are two names for the same document
The Ordinance is the primary law; the Regulations are secondary legislation that spells it out in detail
The Regulations are the primary law; the Ordinance is the detail
questions.explain: The Traffic Ordinance is primary legislation of the Knesset; the Traffic Regulations are secondary legislation that spell out the rules in detail — speeds, right of way, equipment and more.

questions.q: A uniformed police officer gives an instruction at a junction that conflicts with the sign posted there. What should the driver do?
options: Drive however is convenient for them
Obey the sign, because it is more permanent
Stop and wait for the police officer to leave
Obey the police officer — their instruction prevails even when it conflicts with regulations or signs
questions.explain: Under regulation 23, a road user must obey a police officer's instructions even when they conflict with regulations, signs or other general instructions.

questions.q: What is the correct order of priority at a junction that has both a traffic light and a sign?
options: A sign always overrides a traffic light
A sign and a traffic light are always equal, and the driver chooses whichever is clearer to them
There is no order of priority — the driver chooses
A traffic light overrides a sign, and both are subject to the instructions of a police officer or inspector directing traffic at the spot
questions.explain: The practical order of priority is: a police officer or inspector directing traffic ← a traffic light ← a sign ← the regulations' default rules.

questions.q: Who is authorised to place a portable sign on a road and give it the standing of a lawfully placed sign?
options: A police officer
Any citizen who wants to warn other drivers
Any owner of a commercial vehicle
Only a local authority employee who is not an inspector
questions.explain: Regulation 23(c) states that a portable sign placed on a road by a police officer is treated as a lawfully placed sign.

questions.q: Who is responsible for managing the points register and issuing driving and vehicle licences?
options: The local signing authority
The licensing authority (Ministry of Transport)
The police
The traffic court alone
questions.explain: The licensing authority is the body that issues driving and vehicle licences and manages the register of offences and violations, including points.
